articles.title: I Asked 4 Chefs To Name the Best Pasta, and They All Said the Same Brand
articles.summary: It’s widely available and affordable.
articles.body:
Barilla is the preferred brand of dry pasta among our panel of food experts.

They give a thumbs-up to its consistent quality and taste, and also mention the variety of shapes and healthy options.

I'm not a fussy pasta eater—I love all pasta for its carbs, versatility, and tastiness. My pantry is stocked with a wide variety of pasta shapes and styles. I spend too much time pairing the right pasta shape with my sauce—I want it to hold the sauce exactly right. I'm also a sucker for new-to-me pasta shapes. But when I choose pasta at the grocery store, I tend to let the shape influence me, and I don't reach for one specific brand. But should I?

I asked chefs for their favorite dried pastas, and to my surprise, one brand rose to the top.

Dan Pelosi: Best known as @grossypelosi , author of the cookbook Let's Eat: 101 Recipes to Fill Your Heart & Home

Jamie Milne: Teacher-turned-recipe developer for Everything Delish

Lucy Simon: Food & Wine special projects editor and wine, spirits, and food writer

Laura Banks: Health and nutrition coach @laura.b.healthy

The Best Dry Pasta, According to the Experts

The unanimous choice among the experts is Barilla .

Dan expresses his fondness for Barilla, saying, "Barilla, for sure! I love them not only because the pasta cooks perfectly every time but also because I know I can count on them to have all my favorite nostalgic shapes that were part of my Italian American upbringing, like ditalini, orecchiette, and tri-color rotini!" Dan's enthusiasm highlights Barilla's ability to evoke cherished memories through its various shapes.

Jamie has a special place in her heart for Barilla, particularly their rigatoni. She appreciates the consistent quality and taste, making Barilla her go-to brand for creating delicious pasta dishes.

Lucy keeps it simple yet practical: "Truly nothing fancy—I buy Barilla pasta! I find noodles don't fall apart when boiled, which happens often with more affordable grocery store brands. The noodles stay bouncy yet tender without being mealy."

And Laura loves the healthy options Barilla offers. "I almost always use Barilla! I love the whole grain, chickpea, and red lentil noodles they make because of the simple ingredients." Laura's endorsement shows that Barilla caters to those seeking healthier alternatives without sacrificing taste.

Now I'm ready to shop for one of my favorite dinners, a slightly grown-up version of the beloved butter noodles of my childhood—add parm and freshly cracked pepper, please!

articles.title: Irã derrubou dois drones militares dos EUA nos últimos dias, diz TV  | G1
articles.standfirst: Prejuízo estimado às forças dos EUA é da ordem de US$ 8 milhões (R$ 41,2 milhões). Comando Central das Forças Armadas dos EUA não comentou episódios.
articles.summary: Prejuízo estimado às forças dos EUA é da ordem de US$ 8 milhões (R$ 41,2 milhões). Comando Central das Forças Armadas dos EUA não comentou episódios.
articles.body:
Drone militar MQ-1 Predator durante missão no Afeganistãoem 2008, em imagem divulgada pela Força Aérea dos EUA — Foto: Lt. Col. Leslie Pratt/U.S. Air Force

As forças do Irã derrubaram ao menos dois drones militares americanos MQ-1, de acordo com autoridades que falaram com a rede de TV CBS. A reportagem foi publicada pelo site do canal nesta quinta-feira (17).

Os modelos MQ-1 são tipicamente usados como aeronaves espiãs e de reconhecimento, mas também podem carregar mísseis e empregadas em missões de ataque.

Não se sabe se os drones abatidos são da variante Predator, mais antiga, bastante usada nas guerras do Iraque e do Afeganistão, ou da variante Gray Eagle, maior e mais moderna. Considerando que ambas sejam do primeiro modelo, o prejuízo estimado às forças dos EUA é da ordem de US$ 8 milhões (R$ 41,2 milhões).

Uma das questões debatidas em Washington a respeito do envolvimento dos EUA na Guerra do Irã é o custo aos cofres do país.

Segundo um relatório do Escritório Orçamentário do Congresso, só o prejuízo com a perda de 24 drones do modelo MQ-9 Reapers na guerra totaliza US$ 720 milhões, ou R$ 3,7 bilhões.

Questionado pela CBS, o Comando Central das Forças Armadas dos EUA não comentou episódios.

articles.title: Justiça manda consórcio manter serviços do Poupatempo em 3 unidades  | G1
articles.standfirst: A decisão atende a um pedido do Governo do Estado e prevê multa diária de R$ 200 mil por unidade em caso de descumprimento.
articles.summary: A decisão atende a um pedido do Governo do Estado e prevê multa diária de R$ 200 mil por unidade em caso de descumprimento.
articles.body:
Palácio Guanabara — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A Justiça do Rio determinou que o consórcio responsável pelo Poupatempo mantenha os serviços nas unidades de Bangu, na Zona Oeste da capital, em Duque de Caxias e em São João de Meriti, na Baixada Fluminense. A decisão atende a um pedido do Governo do Estado e prevê multa diária de R$ 200 mil por unidade em caso de descumprimento.

O Consórcio RJ Cidadão havia comunicado ao governo que poderia suspender os serviços caso não recebesse um saldo contratual que, segundo as empresas, estava em aberto.

Na decisão, a juíza Alessandra Cristina Tufvesson de Campos Melo considerou que a paralisação poderia prejudicar milhares de pessoas, inclusive usuários com atendimentos agendados.

As unidades oferecem serviços como emissão de documentos, habilitação e serviços relacionados a veículos, trabalho e emprego, assistência social e defesa do consumidor.

O governo afirma que uma auditoria identificou divergências nos números de atendimentos apresentados pelo consórcio. Segundo o Estado, em junho, as empresas informaram ter realizado 845.086 atendimentos, enquanto os órgãos parceiros do programa validaram 261.783.

O contrato prevê pagamento de R$ 24,20 por atendimento. De acordo com o governo, a diferença entre os valores cobrados e os serviços efetivamente validados chegou a cerca de R$ 15 milhões somente em junho.

A Justiça afirmou que os documentos apresentados pelo Estado levantam dúvidas sobre a quantidade de atendimentos efetivamente realizados e, consequentemente, sobre os valores devidos ao consórcio.

articles.title: Buracos quebram veículos e obrigam trator a puxar ônibus em Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Situação foi agravada após temporais atingirem a cidade. No bairro Estoril, um motorista relatou gasto de R$ 7,5 mil com manutenção por causa das más condições do asfalto.
articles.summary: Situação foi agravada após temporais atingirem a cidade.
articles.body:
Buracos em vias de diversos pontos de Piracicaba (SP) têm sido alvo de reclamação dos moradores. Segundo as denúncias recebidas pela EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, pelo menos quatro bairros são afetados.

Rodnei Senicato passa com frequência pelo Bairro Estoril, um dos mais afetados pelos buracos, e conta que já foi prejudicado financeiramente pela má condição do asfalto.

"Complicado porque eu gastei nessa caminhonete e em um outro carro que eu tenho. Já deu acho que uns R$ 7,5 mil só de manutenção mecânica em função da estrada", explica.

Além do prejuízo financeiro, o grande número de buracos nas ruas aumenta também o risco de acidentes. Valdir José Satini, outro morador, fala que presencia acidentes no local frequentemente.

"Muito difícil. Aqui várias vezes já tive que pegar trator para tirar o ônibus que cai em valeta, fica encalhado na época de chuva", relata.

Força da chuva levou acostamento de rua em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo / EPTV

Os fortes temporais que atingiram a região também contribuíram para abrir ainda mais as crateras. Em uma rua do bairro Estoril, o acostamento de terra foi levado pela força da água.

Apesar disso, os buracos causados pela chuva não são o único risco com o qual a população precisa lidar. O Bairro Santa Terezinha, por exemplo, conta com aberturas feitas para manutenção na rua, que, segundo moradores, já duram há mais de 15 dias sem progresso.

A Avenida das Ondas também exige atenção dos motoristas. O caminhoneiro Fábio Fernando passa diariamente pelo trecho e precisa reduzir a velocidade para não danificar o veículo.

"Todos os dias a gente está passando por aqui e é essa situação. Muita cratera, estraga o molejo do caminhão. É difícil transitar aqui nessa via aqui."

Questionada pela EPTV , a Prefeitura de Piracicaba informou que a Avenida das Ondas deve passar por manutenção até o fim de setembro.

Nos demais pontos, a administração informou que faz ações de tapa-buraco de forma continua de acordo com a solicitação dos moradores pelo número 156 e que estuda um novo pacote de recapeamento para atender a cidade.

Moradores de Piracicaba denunciam prejuízos sofridos por causa de buracos na região — Foto: Edijan Del Santo / EPTV

articles.title: VÍDEO: registro raro mostra cachorro-vinagre em parque conservado  | G1
articles.standfirst: Espécie rara foi registrada por câmeras de monitoramento no Parque Sesc Serra Azul, em Rosário Oeste, e também em outras duas áreas de conservação de MT; Veja curiosidades da espécie.
articles.summary: Espécie rara foi registrada por câmeras de monitoramento no Parque Sesc Serra Azul, em Rosário Oeste, e também em outras duas áreas de conservação de MT; Veja curiosidades.
articles.body:
Um cachorro-vinagre, uma das espécies mais raras da fauna brasileira , foi registrado no Parque Sesc Serra Azul, em Rosário Oeste , a 133 km de Cuiabá, neste emana. O animal foi flagrado por câmeras de monitoramento remoto e também identificado em pesquisas científicas realizadas na área de conservação, que tem cerca de 5 mil hectares.

Nas imagens, é possível vê-lo correndo sozinho entre as áreas de mata do parque (assista acima) . Segundo o Sesc, o animal já foi registrado nas três áreas de conservação do Polo Socioambiental Sesc Pantanal, localizadas nos biomas Pantanal e Cerrado .

Além de raro, o animal tem uma característica curiosa que pode ser descoberta pelo próprio nome: o forte odor da urina é o que deu origem ao termo cachorro-vinagre . O cachorro-vinagre usa a urina para marcar território . Para isso, pode se apoiar nas patas dianteiras e erguer as patas traseiras, direcionando o xixi para árvores, pedras e outras superfícies.

A posição ajuda a espécie a deixar a marca em locais mais altos. Já o forte odor da urina, semelhante ao de vinagre, deu origem ao nome popular do animal . Também conhecido como cachorro-do-mato-vinagre, o animal é um dos menores canídeos do Brasil e mede entre 57 e 75 centímetros.

O cachorro-vinagre é considerado vulnerável pelo Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade (ICMBio) . Um dos desafios para a preservação da espécie é a falta de informações sobre as populações que vivem em áreas naturais.

Como o animal é discreto e difícil de observar, as câmeras de monitoramento ajudam pesquisadores a identificar sua presença e estudar seus hábitos.

Apesar de difícil de observar, o cachorro-vinagre foi registrado nas três áreas de conservação do Polo Socioambiental Sesc Pantanal , em Mato Grosso. Além do Parque Sesc Serra Azul, no Cerrado, a espécie foi identificada na Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural (RPPN) Sesc Pantanal e no Parque Sesc Baía das Pedras, no Pantanal mato-grossense.

As três áreas de conservação somam 117 mil hectares nos biomas Pantanal e Cerrado. Os espaços são destinados à conservação da biodiversidade e ao desenvolvimento de ações ambientais, científicas, culturais e educativas.

Além do cachorro-vinagre, o Parque Sesc Serra Azul já registrou outras 15 espécies ameaçadas de extinção, entre elas o tamanduá-bandeira, o lobo-guará, o gavião-real e a onça-pintada.

O cachorro-vinagre costuma viver e caçar em grupos, embora também possa ser encontrado sozinho. A estratégia ajuda os animais a capturar presas maiores. A alimentação é composta principalmente por pequenos vertebrados, mas o grupo também pode caçar tatus, cutias, pacas e catetos.

A espécie também conversa bastante: o cachorro-vinagre possui diferentes vocalizações e é considerada bastante comunicativa.

A gestação também é curiosa: dura entre 60 e 83 dias, e cada ninhada pode ter de um a seis filhotes. O macho também participa dos cuidados com a prole.

O cachorro-vinagre é considerado vulnerável pelo Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade (ICMBio). — Foto: Sesc Pantanal

articles.title: Enfermeira é agredida por paciente dentro de hospital em Miami  | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem agrediu outros quatro profissionais antes de avançar contra enfermeira; vítima vai pedir RS$ 26 milhões ao hospital por suposta falha na segurança.
articles.summary: Profissional foi atingida várias vezes na cabeça e e derrubada no chão; Adovago diz que vítima vai pedir R$ 26 milhões.
articles.body:
Uma enfermeira foi agredida na cabeça várias vezes por um paciente dentro do pronto-socorro do Jackson Memorial Hospital, em Miami, nos Estados Unidos . O ataque aconteceu em 30 de maio e foi registrado por câmeras de segurança.

As imagens mostram o homem, identificado pela polícia como Rubin Wenyou, de 44 anos, perseguindo outra profissional pelo setor de emergência. Ele atinge um funcionário e, em seguida, vira-se contra a enfermeira Yanira Equileor.

Yanira aparece nas imagens sendo atingida várias vezes na cabeça. Ela cai no chão enquanto outros funcionários conseguem conter o suspeito. Em outro trecho da gravação, colegas ajudam a enfermeira a se levantar.

Segundo Michael Pizzi, advogado de Yanira, a profissional sofreu ferimentos na cabeça, no pescoço, na coluna e nas costas, além de hematomas em diferentes partes do corpo.

A defesa afirma que Yanira pretende processar o Jackson Memorial Hospital em US$ 5 milhões (cerca de R$ 26 milhões) por negligência na supervisão e na segurança do local.

Hospital diz que havia agentes de segurança

O Jackson Health, sistema responsável pelo hospital, não comentou diretamente a investigação. Em comunicado, afirmou que quatro profissionais de segurança pública ficam designados para o pronto-socorro do Jackson Memorial 24 horas por dia, sete dias por semana.

O hospital também informou que dois policiais do escritório do xerife do condado de Miami-Dade, que estavam de folga, permanecem no campus em tempo integral.

Em outra declaração, o Jackson Health afirmou que o primeiro agente de segurança chegou ao local poucos segundos após o início do ataque e que outros profissionais foram enviados em seguida. Segundo o hospital, os funcionários envolvidos receberam apoio e atendimento após o episódio.

O advogado de Yanira afirmou ainda que precisou entrar com uma ação judicial contra o hospital e o escritório do xerife de Miami-Dade para obter a divulgação das imagens de segurança. O escritório do xerife disse que não comenta processos judiciais em andamento.

Direção do Jackson Memorial Hospital, em Miami, nos EUA, afirmou que haviam quatro seguranças no lugar — Foto: Reprodução: NBC

articles.title: Obras interditam trecho da Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Intervenção faz parte da ampliação do saneamento da capital e também alcança bairros das zonas Norte e Centro-Norte (veja a lista na reportagem).
articles.summary: Interdição parcial acontece entre os dias 14 e 19 de setembro, das 7h30 às 18h. Outros pontos da cidade também terão intervenções
articles.body:
Obras interditam trecho da Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco em Teresina; veja período e horários — Foto: TV Clube

A Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco, em Teresina , está parcialmente interditada até sábado (19) por causa de obras de ampliação da rede de esgoto. Os serviços começaram na segunda-feira (14) e são realizados diariamente, das 7h30 às 18h.

Durante esse período, o trânsito na região deve sofrer alterações. Motoristas que passam pelo local precisam redobrar a atenção e seguir a sinalização instalada na via.

Segundo a Águas de Teresina, a obra faz parte do cronograma de ampliação da rede de esgoto da capital. A concessionária orienta motoristas e pedestres a redobrarem a atenção ao passar pelo trecho interditado e, sempre que possível, utilizarem rotas alternativas.

Além da Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco, outras vias das zonas Norte e Centro-Norte de Teresina também receberão obras nos próximos dias. As equipes vão trabalhar simultaneamente em ruas e avenidas dos bairros Primavera, Buenos Aires, Mocambinho e Água Mineral.

*Yngridy Vieira, estagiária sob supervisão de Ilanna Serena.

articles.title: Advogado de Campo Grande aprovado para juiz recorre ao STF | G1
articles.standfirst: Autista, Márcio Almeida passou em vaga para PcD, mas foi considerado inapto pelo próprio TJSC; caso discute adaptações no trabalho.
articles.summary: Autista, Márcio Almeida passou em vaga para PcD, mas foi considerado inapto pelo próprio TJSC; caso discute adaptações no trabalho.
articles.body:
Autista tem candidatura barrada em concurso do TJMS — Foto: Reprodução

O caso do advogado Márcio Leonardo Almeida das Virgens, de 30 anos, natural de Campo Grande , chegou ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) depois que ele foi aprovado para atuar como juiz leigo em Santa Catarina, mas acabou considerado inapto pela Junta Médica do próprio Tribunal de Justiça de Santa Catarina (TJSC).

Márcio concorreu a uma vaga reservada para pessoas com deficiência (PcD) e havia sido habilitado nas etapas anteriores do processo seletivo. A situação mudou após a avaliação médica do tribunal, que reconheceu o diagnóstico de Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) e o enquadramento como pessoa com deficiência, mas concluiu que ele não poderia exercer a função.

A decisão é contestada pelo advogado na Justiça. Segundo documentos apresentados por ele no processo, três avaliações psiquiátricas apontaram capacidade para exercer as atividades de juiz leigo, desde que fossem adotadas adaptações consideradas razoáveis.

A discussão chegou ao STF por meio da Reclamação Constitucional (Rcl) 99.199, sob relatoria do ministro Gilmar Mendes.

Campo-grandense conseguiu manter a vaga reservada

Depois de ser considerado inapto, Márcio recorreu à Justiça. Segundo o candidato, uma decisão de primeira instância determinou a reserva da vaga enquanto o caso é analisado e também ordenou a realização de uma perícia psiquiátrica independente para esclarecer a divergência entre os documentos médicos.

O Ministério Público também se manifestou no processo. Conforme relatado pelo candidato, o órgão apontou que a avaliação biopsicossocial prevista no edital não teria sido realizada integralmente e defendeu a nulidade do ato que declarou a inaptidão, além de uma nova avaliação por equipe multiprofissional.

A reserva da vaga, no entanto, não significa que Márcio já possa exercer a função.

Em 25 de agosto, a 5ª Câmara de Direito Público do TJSC negou um pedido para que ele começasse imediatamente a trabalhar enquanto o processo continua. O colegiado entendeu que a manutenção da vaga reservada seria suficiente, por enquanto, para preservar a possibilidade de uma futura designação.

Laudos médicos apontaram capacidade para o trabalho

Antes da decisão da Junta Médica, Márcio passou por três avaliações psiquiátricas. Uma delas foi feita por uma profissional credenciada pelo próprio TJSC e analisou especificamente sua capacidade para desempenhar as atribuições de juiz leigo.

Segundo os documentos apresentados no processo, os exames indicaram que o diagnóstico de TEA não comprometeria funções como raciocínio lógico, atenção, memória, julgamento, tomada de decisões e desempenho em atividades intelectuais.

O edital previa que as atividades de juiz leigo seriam realizadas de forma integralmente remota.

Os profissionais que avaliaram Márcio recomendaram algumas adaptações, entre elas a redução de estímulos sonoros, controle de temperatura do ambiente ou possibilidade de trabalho em home office, encaminhamento preferencial de demandas por meios eletrônicos e liberação para psicoterapia semanal.

Uma das avaliações, feita por profissional credenciada pelo próprio tribunal, concluiu que ele estava apto para exercer a função considerando essas adaptações.

Junta médica chegou a uma conclusão diferente

Apesar dos laudos anteriores, a Junta Médica Oficial do TJSC considerou Márcio inapto especificamente para o exercício da função de juiz leigo.

O parecer reconheceu que ele tem TEA e se enquadra como pessoa com deficiência, mas afirmou que não seria possível conciliar as limitações decorrentes da deficiência com o exercício adequado da função a longo prazo.

O candidato questiona, porém, quais seriam essas limitações e por que as adaptações indicadas nas avaliações anteriores não seriam suficientes.

Para Márcio, a discussão não é sobre reduzir as exigências do cargo, mas sobre avaliar sua capacidade individual para exercer as atividades com os recursos necessários.

“Não peço que o Judiciário flexibilize a função por eu ser autista; peço apenas que o próprio Judiciário aplique a mim as regras de inclusão e adaptação razoável que ele exige de toda a sociedade.”

A principal questão do processo é saber como deve ser feita a avaliação de uma pessoa com deficiência que foi aprovada para uma função pública, especialmente quando existem laudos médicos divergentes.

A Lei Brasileira de Inclusão estabelece que a avaliação da deficiência, quando necessária, deve considerar não apenas o diagnóstico, mas também fatores pessoais e ambientais, limitações para realizar atividades e possíveis restrições de participação. A legislação também prevê adaptações razoáveis para garantir igualdade de oportunidades.

A mesma lei estabelece que a pessoa com deficiência tem direito ao trabalho em condições acessíveis e inclusivas e proíbe restrições ao trabalho ou discriminação em razão da deficiência, inclusive nas etapas de recrutamento, seleção, contratação e admissão.

No caso do autismo, a legislação federal determina que a pessoa com Transtorno do Espectro Autista é considerada pessoa com deficiência para todos os efeitos legais.

A controvérsia chegou ao Supremo por meio da Reclamação Constitucional 99.199, apresentada por Márcio em agosto. O processo está sob relatoria do ministro Gilmar Mendes.

A discussão envolve a decisão que impediu o exercício imediato da função e os critérios usados para avaliar a capacidade do candidato.

Enquanto o processo não é definido, Márcio continua com a vaga reservada, mas sem poder exercer a função de juiz leigo.

O TJSC foi procurado para comentar o caso e explicar os critérios utilizados pela Junta Médica, mas não havia respondido até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: First minister: A pay rise of more than £2k for MLAs is 'grotesque'
articles.summary: The proposals follow MLAs being awarded an almost 27% uplift in their annual wages in April - a rise of more than £14,000.
articles.body:
A pay rise of more than £2,000 for Northern Ireland Assembly members (MLAs) is "grotesque", the first minister has said.

The proposals planned for next year would bring MLAs annual salary to £69,216.

The increase will take effect from the first sitting day of the new assembly mandate next May, under draft proposals by Stormont's Independent Remuneration Board.

Speaking to the media at Stormont, she said: "This issue of wages is not in my agenda. It's not something we've pushed for."

"It's not something we've asked for and actually I think it looks quite grotesque in the climate that we're in."

The proposals follow MLAs being awarded an almost 27% uplift in their annual wages in April - a rise of more than £14,000.

A spokesman for the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) said the party has "no input" in setting MLA salaries.

"At the present time we are focused on the need for a fair and stable funding settlement for Northern Ireland so that hardworking nurses, doctors and other frontline workers are properly rewarded for their work," they added.

Alliance MLA Eóin Tennyson told the media on Thursday that the pay rise "smacks of being completely out of touch with where the public are".

"We are more than adequately paid," Tennyson said, adding that he sees no "coherent" argument for the rise.

The leader of the Ulster Unionist Party, Jon Burrows, said "our nurses need their pay rise before our politicians".

He added that, while he respects the independence of the remuneration board, he feels there is a sense of "unease" around MLAs' value for money.

"We haven't set a multi-year budget, we haven't got a budget of any sort, and people think that Stormont is under-performing."

Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) leader Claire Hanna said a pay rise is "going to be impossible for people to stomach".

"Those who are doing their job and trying to do their job should be properly remunerated for it but unfortunately some are prevented from doing that by the dysfunction".

Alan Lowry, chair of the board, said the 27% rise was a "corrective measure" after years of no substantial rises - but future increases would be expected to "reflect inflationary and other pay trends".

"MLAs carry out a wide range of important duties, from representing constituents and scrutinising legislation to holding ministers and departments to account," he said.

He said it was "right that their remuneration recognises the complexity and importance of those responsibilities, while ensuring that financial considerations do not discourage people from seeking elected office".

He added: "As we look ahead to the assembly election next year and the start of a new mandate, it is important that we put in place a structured and transparent mechanism that links MLA pay to changes in earnings in Northern Ireland.

"This approach ensures that pay remains aligned with wider developments in society, while providing certainty and maintaining public confidence in the process."

Under the proposals, while the basic MLA salary will increase in line with earnings growth, payments for different office holders will remain unchanged throughout the 2027-32 mandate.

Lowry said: "In making this draft determination, we are increasing the transparency of our decision-making and making it easier for the public to understand how remuneration is structured.

"The board will now consult with our statutory consultees - MLAs, the Assembly Commission and the Assembly Members' Pension Trustees, over a four-week period.

"It is also inviting views from members of the public during this same timeframe.

"After that, we will take some time to reflect on the responses received and present a final determination to the Assembly Commission for publication and implementation."

The proposals come as Stormont ministers face pressure from trade unions over public sector pay, with some health workers taking part in strike action in recent months.

The health minister at the time said he was unable to implement pay awards in the absence of an agreed Stormont budget.

Northern Ireland's four-party devolved government has yet to set a budget five months into the financial year.

Stormont departments are facing a shortfall of up to £1.6bn, according to a spending watchdog.

With no agreed plan, public services have been operating under contingency arrangements.

The parties have been holding talks with the UK government and Treasury in recent months in a bid secure additional funding.

Maria Morgan NIPSA Deputy General Secretary said it was surprising in the context of the rise of the 27% and the £14,000.

"I think it will go down very badly with our members," she said.

"I think it will go down very badly with the public given we've just been announced significant cuts in the health service, significant cuts in education...right across the public sector our members are waiting for their pay."

At Westminster, MPs earn £98,599 a year while members of the Dáil (lower house of the Irish parliament) earn €119,467 (£102,334).

What is the Independent Remuneration Board?

The three-member panel was set up with the sole remit of setting MLAs' pay and pension entitlements.

The body replaced the Independent Financial Review Panel (IFRP), which had made decisions on both the wages and expenses provisions for MLAs.

However the tenures of its three members ended in 2016 and they were never replaced.

MLAs at the time took issue with some of the rules the panel imposed, including limits on salaries for constituency office staff and other matters such as office signage.

The bill which established the Independent Remuneration Board was backed by the Assembly Commission - a body which handles the running of Parliament Buildings and involves representatives of Stormont's main parties.

But some MLAs criticised the bill, arguing it would lead to assembly members receiving significant pay rises.

articles.title: Portsmouth RNLI lifeboat station off service after anti-migrant protest
articles.summary: The RNLI says it hopes to have the lifeboat station operational again as soon as possible.
articles.body:
Portsmouth's lifeboat station remains temporarily out of service following anti-migrant protests.

Protesters blocked roads in the city on 6 September after about 120 people arrived at the Eastney Landing ferry port area following a Channel small boat crossing. The RNLI helped bring them ashore.

The RNLI also said it helped to ensure the safety of anti-migrant demonstrators who went into the sea.

Following the protest, the charity's chief executive said staff had faced "unacceptable" online and physical abuse . The lifeboat station was taken out of service on 10 September, meanwhile, abuse aimed at volunteers also forced the lifeboat museum in Poole to shut for several days.

The RNLI said: "Search and rescue cover continues to be provided through established contingency arrangements, including flank RNLI stations and other declared assets.

"We hope to have the lifeboat station back on service as soon as possible."

After abuse was directed at its crews tasked to assist the incident, its chief executive issued a statement .

Peter Sparkes said: "Recent events have generated deliberate misinformation and a misunderstanding about the RNLI – our purpose, our tasking, and particularly our lifesaving work in the Channel.

"Sadly, as a result, some of our volunteers and staff have been the subject of online and, in the worst cases, physical abuse.

"The RNLI's people represent the very best in our society, they selflessly give up their time to keep others safe."

He added: "Stand by them, not against them and their families. I am extremely proud of and grateful for their vital lifesaving work."

The protest in Portsmouth followed a separate demonstration the previous day, in which hundreds of masked "stop the boats" protesters brought the Port of Dover to a standstill .

The protests led the RNLI to also review its security procedures. As part of this, volunteers were told to consider not wearing RNLI-branded clothing in some circumstances while representing the charity.

articles.title: How far will Egypt go to help Saudi Arabia secure the Red Sea?
articles.summary: Regional analysts highlight the growing security alignment between Cairo and Riyadh amid escalating Red Sea tensions.
articles.body:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s latest meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi this week came at a highly sensitive moment for both countries.

Mere days before Tuesday’s meeting, Iran-aligned Houthi rebels seized Yemen’s Red Sea coast, gaining significant control over the Bab al-Mandeb strait, the southern gateway to the Suez Canal.

This precipitated a Saudi air campaign over Yemen and repeated attacks by the Houthis on the kingdom’s oil infrastructure.

Analysts say Riyadh is looking for help to protect the kingdom and Red Sea shipping, and that Egypt, whose Suez Canal revenue depends on the same traffic, is an obvious partner.

The deepening bilateral relationship carries significant implications for the region, from the conflicts in Yemen and Sudan to Egypt’s close ties with the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia’s new defence pact with Turkiye and Pakistan.

Abdel Monem Said, a member of Egypt’s Senate who is close to decision-making circles in Cairo, told Al Jazeera the visit had political, economic, strategic and military dimensions.

He said it came as Iran escalated regional conflicts through what he called its proxies, chief among them the Houthis. Their advance directly threatened Egypt’s economy and the Suez Canal, he said.

Said stressed the need for joint strategic and military thinking between Egypt and Saudi Arabia that would act as a strong deterrent against Iran-backed groups from Iraq to Yemen.

He added that Egypt is eager to prevent Iran and its allies from imposing control over the region, especially over maritime traffic in the Red Sea, given the direct repercussions this has for the Suez Canal.

Andreas Krieg, a senior lecturer at King’s College London, said Cairo increasingly sees one continuous security space stretching from the Suez Canal to Bab al-Mandeb.

If that southern gateway becomes unreliable, he said, Egypt stands to lose shipping, hard currency and strategic leverage.

“I do think Cairo now has a very strong interest in substantive cooperation with Saudi Arabia on Red Sea security,” he told Al Jazeera over email.

In the lead-up to the meeting, the chairman of the Arab Affairs Committee in Egypt’s House of Representatives, Mohamed Salah Abu Hemila, told Al Jazeera that the Saudi crown prince’s visit may produce a new roadmap for political and strategic cooperation on a number of Arab and regional issues.

The alliance between the two nations would serve as the cornerstone for building a new Arab order — more robust, cohesive, and capable of safeguarding its interests and defending its just causes, he said.

The foremost issues would be Red Sea security and freedom of international navigation, but they would also include the Palestinian cause and the situations in Yemen, Libya and Sudan.

A statement released by el-Sisi’s office after the meeting also affirmed that “relations between Egypt and Saudi Arabia can only be exemplary within the Arab framework,” and linked Egyptian and Gulf security.

Tarek Fahmy, professor of international relations at Cairo University, told Al Jazeera that Saudi Arabia is increasingly acting within an Arab framework after the United States’s reaction to the Houthi escalations fell short of what the kingdom expected. Reports suggest that Saudi Arabia asked the Trump administration for military help in combatting the Iran-backed group, but that Trump refused. Neither Saudi Arabia nor the US has officially commented on these reports.

No details of specific military cooperation between the two countries were announced during or after the meeting.

However, Egypt is already a party to a Saudi-led coalition for Red Sea maritime security launched in August. The grouping was created as a consequence of international fears that the Houthis could close Bab al-Mandeb while Iran had the Strait of Hormuz choked off.

The coalition, whose founding document stresses it is purely defensive in nature, has not taken military action against the Houthis so far. The rebel group, too, has not taken measures to shut down shipping after its recent advances.

Krieg says Saudi-Egyptian military cooperation is likely to entail intelligence sharing, maritime surveillance, protection of commercial shipping and greater coordination around the Red Sea.

But there is a “very hard ceiling” on how far Egypt will involve itself inside Yemen, he said. “The Egyptian preference will be to defend the maritime system without becoming responsible for Yemen.”

Historical memory likely plays a role in that preference. In the 1960s, Egyptian leader Gamal Abdel Nasser sent tens of thousands of Egyptian soldiers to participate in the North Yemen Civil War, a long and costly endeavour that yielded few results and many casualties.

“Yemen taught Egypt that an apparently limited intervention can become a strategic trap very quickly,” Krieg said.

It’s no surprise that the two nations should seek to deepen cooperation at this moment, say analysts. The Iran war is only the latest – and perhaps greatest – in a series of regional crises that the two states have found themselves roughly aligned on.

In January, weeks before the war began, el-Sisi met Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud in Cairo. Afterwards, the Egyptian presidency said the two countries held “identical” views on solutions to regional crises that focus on preserving the unity and sovereignty of states.

This was reiterated on Tuesday, when the two sides “stressed that any threat to Sudan’s unity and territorial integrity poses a danger to the collective security of Egypt, Saudi Arabia and all countries of the region”, according to Egypt’s State Information Service.

“Both are deeply uncomfortable with the fragmentation of states and the rise of militias, separatist movements and externally sponsored sub-state actors,” Krieg said. “You can see that in Sudan, Libya, Somalia and increasingly Yemen.”

However, this strategic vision for the region has run contrary to Abu Dhabi’s preferences and policies.

That pre-war meeting between el-Sisi and Prince Faisal came only days after Saudi Arabia launched strikes on a United Arab Emirates-backed separatist group in Yemen, which was widely received as a repudiation of Abu Dhabi.

The UAE is long faced accusations of sponsoring the Rapid Support Forces rebel group in Sudan, driving a devastating civil war that has negative ramifications for Egyptian security. Cairo has supported Khartoum’s efforts to combat the group and restore its sovereignty. The UAE has rejected accusations that it has provided military, logistical, financial or political support to the RSF.

At the same time, the UAE is far and away the largest investor in the Egyptian economy. In 2025, its net investments in the country were more than double that of the second-biggest investor, the United States.

“This is where the Saudi-UAE rivalry becomes difficult for Egypt. Cairo does not want to choose between Saudi Arabia and the UAE,” Krieg says.

Instead, Krieg expects Egypt to compartmentalise, siding with Riyadh on security matters while preserving its economic relationship with Abu Dhabi.

Riyadh “does not need Cairo to publicly attack Abu Dhabi”, he said, but to use its geography, intelligence and influence to make certain regional strategies harder.

Saudi Arabia’s urgent need to contain the fallout from the US-Iran war has led it to embrace an increasing number of partners and allies.

Since the war began, it has signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement to include Turkiye in a bilateral mutual defence treaty it had with Pakistan.

It has organised a multilateral maritime security coalition for the Red Sea, sought assurances from the United States and the European Union and signed a defence agreement with Ukraine .

These measures, however, have been more form than function, say analysts. They have not deterred Iran and its regional allies from launching direct attacks on the kingdom, nor have they empowered Yemeni allies to keep the Houthis in check.

Tuesday’s meeting seemed to tacitly acknowledge the lack of a ready military solution for Yemen. Egypt expressed support for “efforts to reach a comprehensive and sustainable political solution to the Yemen crisis”.

They may, however, indicate the kind of security architecture that will emerge once the war is over.

articles.title: Modi’s Jhargram jhalmuri moment goes full circle as stall owner celebrates PM’s birthday
articles.summary: JHARGRAM: A roadside jhalmuri stall in Jhargram shot into the national spotlight after Prime Minister Narendra Modi stopped there during his assembly .
articles.body: JHARGRAM: A roadside jhalmuri stall in Jhargram shot into the national spotlight after Prime Minister Narendra Modi stopped there during his assembly election campaign in April and sampled the popular Bengali snack, with photographs and videos of the encounter quickly going viral on social media.On Thursday, the stall's owner turned the moment into a personal birthday tribute for the Prime Minister, news agency PTI reported.Vikram Kumar Sahu, who runs the Chavan Lal Special Jhalmuri stall near Raj College More, celebrated Modi's birthday at his shop by putting up photographs of their brief encounter, sharing the memory on social media and serving customers larger-than-usual portions of jhalmuri."The Prime Minister came to my shop and had jhalmuri. That moment is unforgettable for me. I wanted to celebrate his birthday here and remember that moment again," Sahu said, wishing Modi good health and a long life.The encounter lasted only a few minutes.PM Modi, travelling between election programmes in Jhargram, stopped at the roadside stall, spoke to Sahu and sampled the snack before leaving.Photographs and videos of the visit, including footage shared from the Prime Minister's social media handles, soon travelled far beyond Jhargram, PTI reported.For Sahu, however, the sudden fame came with an unexpected problem as his modest stall became a destination for people wanting to recreate the Modi moment.Calls poured in, visitors arrived to make reels, and the vendor found himself repeatedly recounting the few minutes that had changed the fortunes and visibility of his shop.Contemporaneous reports said the video crossed 100 million views on Instagram within a day, while searches for "jhalmuri" also surged sharply.For several weeks, jhalmuri became an unlikely visual motif of the BJP's Bengal campaign, with the Modi stop spawning reels, short videos and social media posts around the snack.Jhalmuri also began appearing as a popular offering at BJP programmes, giving the mixture of puffed rice, spices, onions and chillies a new presence during the campaign season.The April campaign was followed by a major electoral change in Bengal, with the BJP winning 207 of the 293 seats for which results were declared, while the Trinamool Congress won 80. The results were declared in May.Jhalmuri, of course, had no ballot paper.But in the weeks around the election, it became one of the campaign's most recognisable and widely replayed flavours, PTI reported.Five months later, the same jhalmuri stall has once again been associated with the Modi moment.On the Prime Minister's birthday, Sahu did not organise an elaborate event.Instead, he returned to the memory that had made his shop famous, served customers jhalmuri and shared photographs once again.From a roadside cone of puffed rice to millions of views, the journey of Sahu's jhalmuri has been an unlikely one.For the vendor behind it, however, the most important part of the story remains those few minutes when a Prime Minister stopped at his little shop.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Melinda French Gates gave $5 million to an Alabama clinic after abortion ban; it quadrupled in size and became a full-service health centre
articles.summary: US News: An Alabama women's healthcare clinic has expanded into a larger health centre with support from a $5 million grant from Melinda French Gates' philanth.
articles.body: An Alabama women's healthcare clinic has expanded into a larger health centre with support from a $5 million grant from Melinda French Gates' philanthropic organisation, Pivotal. WAWC Healthcare in Tuscaloosa previously provided abortion services before Alabama's abortion ban became enforceable following the US Supreme Court's 2022 decision overturning Roe v. Wade. The clinic later reopened with a broader healthcare mission, offering services including pregnancy care, midwifery support and mental health care. Its expansion illustrates how WAWC developed its healthcare model amid changes to abortion access in Alabama, while pursuing its longer-term aim of providing comprehensive services to women and families.Melinda French Gates' $5 million grant helps Alabama clinic expand women's healthcarePivotal's grant supported WAWC Healthcare's reopening and expansion in Tuscaloosa. The clinic developed a broader healthcare model that includes pregnancy care, midwifery services and mental health support. French Gates visited the facility to learn about its services, including its mental health programme. The funding forms part of her wider focus on improving women's healthcare and supporting organisations that address gaps in access to care.The West Alabama Women's Center provided abortion services before the Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization overturned Roe v. Wade in June 2022. Alabama's existing abortion ban subsequently became enforceable. The clinic closed following the change and later reopened with a broader healthcare focus. WAWC Executive Director Robin Marty has also described the organisation's longer-term intention to become a full-spectrum healthcare centre, showing that its expansion was not solely a response to the abortion ban.The new facility is four times the size of the former clinicWAWC Healthcare's new facility in Tuscaloosa opened on April 25, 2026, according to Alabama Reflector. The publication reported that the new location is four times the size of the clinic's former footprint at Jack Warner Parkway. The larger facility provides space for expanded healthcare services and the organisation's mental health wing. Local reporting also described the new centre as having twice as many examination rooms as the previous location.WAWC Healthcare expands maternal and reproductive servicesThe clinic's healthcare services include pregnancy verification, prenatal care, miscarriage management and contraception. Its official website also lists STI and HIV testing and treatment, PrEP and annual examinations. WAWC offers contraception on a sliding scale and states that it does not provide elective abortions. These services reflect the organisation's broader approach to reproductive and general healthcare.Mental health support is a key part of WAWC's expanded services. Fortune reported that French Gates visited the facility to learn about its mental health programmes, including care related to postpartum depression. Local reporting has highlighted the work of counsellor Tamela Hughes-Lawson, whose services support women during pregnancy and after childbirth. The mental health programme forms part of the centre's wider approach to addressing women's healthcare needs.The clinic's growth comes amid Alabama's healthcare challengesWAWC's expansion comes as Alabama continues to face healthcare challenges affecting women and families. Alabama Reflector reported that the clinic previously saw approximately 250 patients per month, most of whom sought abortions. The organisation continued to see substantial demand for healthcare after abortion services were no longer available. Its expansion reflects an effort to provide broader care through maternal healthcare, contraception and mental health services.Melinda French Gates' wider commitment to women's healthThe Alabama clinic is part of Melinda French Gates' wider work in women's healthcare. In June 2026, Pivotal announced a $215 million commitment focused on reproductive health, midlife and menopause, and mental health. The initiative aims to address gaps in women's healthcare through philanthropic funding and partnerships. WAWC's expansion provides a local example of the type of healthcare access and service development highlighted in French Gates' broader philanthropic work.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Salvadorans with TPS don’t know how long their protections will last. ‘Don’t panic,’ advocate says.
articles.summary: José Palma of the National TPS Alliance says wrong paperwork or advice can jeopardize future immigration status, as he argues immigrants here for 25 years should have a “permanent solution.”
articles.body: HOUSTON — José Palma’s face lights up when he remembers leaving El Salvador in 1998 at the age of 23 for the U.S., with the dream of working, learning English and building a family. Twenty-eight years later, his life is divided between paperwork, community hearings, and a family full of love and varying immigration statuses: Palma, who lives in Houston, has U.S. citizen children — two of whom are still young — and a wife who’s a legal permanent resident, and he’s a beneficiary of Temporary Protected Status, which allows eligible immigrants from certain countries to live and work in the U.S. without fear of deportation. As the national coordinator of the National TPS Alliance, Palma has been answering a lot of questions from Salvadorans with TPS: Their immigration protections were set to expire last week, but the Department of Homeland Security announced that Salvadorans will retain TPS protections — including work authorization — for now until an announcement is made at a later date. But there’s uncertainty among Salvadoran TPS holders about what could come next and what happens now with work permits or driver’s licenses that have expired or are about to expire. Immigrants from countries that have lost their TPS designation, including Haiti and Nicaragua, have lost their work permits and ability to be in the U.S. legally, and they face deportation. Palma has lived under TPS protection since 2001. “Everything we’ve built is in danger of collapsing,” he said. “Twenty-five years is not a short time. It’s a lifetime.” Palma said that amid the uncertainty, Salvadoran TPS holders and their families have been dealing with real consequences: People are being asked not to return to work by their employers, families fear the loss of their health insurance and parents are unsure if they will be able to continue driving vehicles in the United States. Advising caution Palma recommended one thing to Salvadoran TPS beneficiaries: “Don’t panic or make decisions based on rumors,” he said. The Trump administration has said that until it announces a decision, Salvadorans with TPS still have protection, so Palma’s advice is “to rely only on official sources, credible community organizations and established media” for accurate information. One of the biggest points of confusion, Palma acknowledged, is whether Salvadoran TPS holders can continue working. “DHS has said that people retain protection, but USCIS guidance for employers indicated that certain automatic work permit extensions were valid until Sept. 9,” Palma said, referring to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. “People should keep their USCIS letters, check their myUSCIS account and seek accredited legal advice before assuming which document applies to their case or employment.” For those who have already received warnings from employers, Palma had this advice: “Do not resign or sign any documents you do not understand. Bring any official notifications you receive from USCIS to your employer and ask human resources to check the agency for updates regarding Form I-9. No one should decide the future of your immigration case based on an unverified comment, social media post or phone call.” Unfortunately, some Salvadoran TPS holders have already been affected. Palma said that people who applied between January and March 2025 to renew their work permits haven’t received them. Some employers have told them not to return to work, and others have told them they can only work until a certain date. “Driver’s licenses depend on immigration status, health insurance can be cut off and loans can be denied — the consequences go far beyond losing immigration protection or a work permit,” he said. If the Trump administration decides to end TPS protections for Salvadorans, people don’t have to leave the country within 60 days, Palma emphasized. “That period is the minimum protection period before a decision can take effect,” he said. “After that, each person must evaluate their case: There may be a family petition, asylum, another legal process or an immigration defense. The recommendation is to seek legal evaluation now and not wait for an emergency.” What to do in the meantime Salvadoran TPS holders should be gathering copies of their work permit, TPS certificate, passport, driver’s license, USCIS receipts, birth and marriage certificates, children’s medical and school records, proof of employment, and tax returns, Palma said. He also said it’s important to identify a licensed immigration attorney or accredited organization. He urged people not to lie on any forms or submit applications for which they don’t qualify or give money to people who promise to “fix” their immigration status. Palma also warned against signing documents without understanding them, giving access to bank accounts or personal information to strangers, or trusting a notary as if they were an immigration lawyer. TPS holders should also avoid any legal problems or issues such as driving under the influence of alcohol, using false documents or committing acts that could jeopardize any future immigration status. When asked what TPS holders should do if they’re stopped or approached by authorities, Palma said the important thing to do is “stay calm.” “Bringing a copy of your identification or immigration documents can be helpful. If it’s an immigration officer, don’t sign any papers without knowing what they contain or without speaking to a lawyer,” he said. “Every case is different, but a signature obtained under duress can have serious immigration consequences.” Temporary status for decades becomes a ‘whole life’ The National TPS Alliance estimates that about 170,000 Salvadorans are directly protected by TPS. However, Palma explained that the actual number of people affected is much higher when one includes U.S. citizen children, spouses, employers, churches, businesses and entire communities. If TPS for Salvadorans is ended, “the impact would be immediate in cleaning, hotels, restaurants, kitchens and construction; there are also Salvadorans with TPS working in transportation, healthcare and professional occupations,” he said. Palma was asked what he tells people who say that TPS is temporary and beneficiaries should return to their countries. He said it’s important to understand the history of the program. “It’s been renewed every 18 months, under both Democratic and Republican administrations, for 25 years. After all this time, we haven’t been given an opportunity to apply for permanent status,” he said. “So, the question is legal, but also moral: If someone has lived in the United States for 25 years with immigration status, is that really temporary? For many, 25 years is a whole life.” “The least we deserve is the opportunity to continue our lives, as we have done all these years, but with permanent immigration status,” Palma said. “I want Democrats and Republicans to take this issue seriously, reach an agreement and find a permanent solution.” An earlier version of this story was first published in Noticias Telemundo.

articles.title: Ghalibaf’s maths missile at Trump decoded: Is Iran fixing US interest rates?
articles.summary: Iran’s speaker mocks US interest rates, citing the Taylor equation amidst rising global oil prices and inflation.
articles.body:
Iran’s missiles and drones have downed dozens of US aircraft, damaged or destroyed hundreds of the United States’ buildings at its bases in the Middle East, and drained its inventories of military equipment worth billions of dollars, the Pentagon conceded earlier this week.

On Wednesday, Tehran unleashed another unlikely weapon in its war against the US: a maths equation.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has also been a lead negotiator during talks between Tehran and Washington at different stages during the past six months, typed out a version of the Taylor equation, a formula used by central banks to determine interest rates, in a post on X loaded with a wartime message.

“Let’s see if a hike could open SOH or produce a single barrel,” he wrote, referring to interest rate hikes and the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway Iran has effectively blocked for global shipping.

“You can’t 25bp [basis points] a chokepoint,” he added, seemingly again referring to the strait. “It’s SOH risk premium, and We set it.”

Hours after Ghalibaf’s post, the US Federal Reserve did raise the benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points.

Early in the war, which was launched by the US and Israel against Iran on February 28, Ghalibaf frequently used financial arguments to mock how the conflict was being conducted by the administration of US President Donald Trump, to point to Iran’s ability to hurt Washington economically unless it changed its approach.

“This is a spectacular bit of agitprop from Iran, a country which, if nothing else in 2026, has demonstrated an impressive ability to needle its US opponent,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group, told Al Jazeera.

But what exactly is Ghalibaf trying to say? What is the Taylor equation, has the Iran war influenced the US interest rate, and does Tehran “set it”, as the parliament speaker has suggested?

What is the Taylor equation that Ghalibaf cited?

The rule is a formula economists use to estimate where a central bank should set interest rates based on inflation and the strength of the economy.

Developed by economist John Taylor in the early 1990s, the rule links the US federal funds rate to inflation and the “output gap” – the difference between actual economic output and its potential.

Interest rate = inflation + 0.5(output gap) + 0.5(inflation − 2%) + 2%.

This means the recommended interest rate rises when inflation moves above the 2 percent target or when economic output exceeds its potential. It falls when inflation weakens or the economy operates below potential.

However, the equation is a benchmark, not a set rule that is strictly followed. Policymakers at the US Federal Reserve weigh other economic factors when setting interest rates.

Is the Iran war a factor in the US interest rate hike?

Trump’s tariffs, the energy shock following the US-Israeli war with Iran, and heavy investment associated with the artificial intelligence boom, taken together, have kept inflationary pressures strong, experts say.

On Wednesday, when the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25bp, it was the first increase in three years.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, in his speech following the rate hike, said renewed fighting between the US and Iran, which has pushed up petrol prices, helped convince Fed officials to support higher rates.

“There’s no hiding from hot spots around the world,” Warsh said.

IG Group’s Beauchamp said, “The Iran war, indirectly, is a huge driver of last night’s hike, though no one wants to admit it.”

“The energy spike has combined with the rise in yields to drive the Fed into a corner with no way out,” he said.

Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at the Wealth Club, said there is “no denying” that Iran’s retaliatory action against the US and its allies across the Gulf region has “intensified concerns about energy supplies and led to hotter inflation forecasts”.

“The ongoing geopolitical turmoil and elevated crude prices certainly were key issues behind the Fed’s decision to hike rates,” she said.

Wealth Club’s Streeter cautioned that while the war in the Middle East and rising oil prices were certainly an element in the Fed’s decision, they weren’t the “only factors at play”.

“The spending might of AI hyperscalers has also pulsed through the veins of the economy, with strong capital investment and resilient domestic demand adding to inflationary pressures, so policymakers will have been looking at the whole picture,” she noted.

“So, while Tehran has arguably had an influence on some of the forces feeding into US monetary policy, particularly through the impact of the conflict on oil supplies and prices, it is not ‘setting’ US interest rates.”

Streeter said the US Federal Reserve was responding to a much broader set of economic conditions.

“Iran’s actions have affected the inflation outlook, but the decision on where to set interest rates ultimately rests with the Federal Reserve, and there are plenty of other data points policymakers use,” she noted.

In March, Iran’s parliamentary speaker repeatedly used social media to comment on markets and energy prices, including mocking efforts by the Trump administration to influence oil futures and arguing that financial manoeuvring could not create “actual fuel” at petrol stations.

Last month, Ghalibaf posted a graphic bearing the phrase “Make America Hungry Again” – a play on Trump’s slogan “Make America Great Again” – together with statistics on food insecurity and hunger in the US. “You can’t cover up defeats with false claims,” he said.

“Ghalibaf’s point is that a US interest rate increase cannot reopen the Strait of Hormuz or replace disrupted oil supplies,” Negar Mortazavi, a senior fellow at the Center for International Policy in Washington, DC, said. “His altered Taylor rule adds Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb to a formula normally concerned with inflation and economic output. He is using the Fed’s own language to argue that the war’s economic costs depend partly on maritime security, which Tehran can affect.”

That is a statement about Iran’s leverage rather than a serious proposal for setting interest rates, she added.

“The timing matters: he posted it as the Fed raised rates by a quarter point. His repeated financial posts are aimed at making the war’s costs legible to a US audience through prices, markets and monetary policy.”

articles.title: West of England's bid to become UK film industry capital
articles.summary: The region, which includes Bristol and Bath, is already the country's third-largest screen hub.
articles.body:
Bosses of the West of England hope to transform the region into the film industry capital of the UK amid a £4.5m funding boost.

The region, which includes Bristol and Bath, is already the country's third-largest screen hub, with huge series including Rivals, The Outlaws, The Other Bennet Sister and Young Sherlock already being filmed in the area.

The new grant scheme, Greenlight West, now aims to attract large productions by helping to cover associated costs, giving the West an edge over other locations.

Helen Godwin, mayor of the West of England, said: "With this new incentive, we're sending a clear message to the sector. We want you to make more magic here."

The scheme, launched by the West of England Combined Authority (Weca), is forecast to generate more than 230 jobs, alongside supporting freelancers, local suppliers, and the wider screen supply chain.

Awards of between £50,000 to £500,000 will be available for "ambitious and commercially viable" screen productions that can demonstrate the impact they will bring in terms of local spend, employment, skills development and other benefits.

Unlike many other incentives offered across the UK, funding is non-recoupable.

Eligible applicants include incoming productions filming in the region, productions made or led by regionally based companies, and productions carrying out significant post-production work locally.

The region's Growth Strategy , launched in September 2025, identified the creative industries as one of five sectors expected to drive economic growth over the next decade.

The new production fund comes alongside separate plans to expand the region's screen infrastructure.

Bristol City Council has also launched a separate £6m bid to expand The Bottle Yard Studios in Hengrove, where productions including Rivals and Broadchurch have been filmed.

Announcing the scheme at Bristol Old Vic earlier, Godwin described the West as "the place to be" for prospective producers.

"We're serious about ramping up our region's credentials as a filming hub even further, to grow this important sector and stimulate more spending, create more jobs and skills opportunities for local people," she said.

"We're here to help you invest, recruit, and train locally and we look forward to harnessing the power that your film and TV production can bring to the country's fastest-growing regional economy."

Rachel Drummond-Hay, chair of the Royal Television Society West of England, added: "Not only will the fund give companies based in the region an edge when it comes to pitching, tendering and financing new projects of scale, it will also help ensure talent stays in the region and new talent continues to be developed."

articles.title: Texas abortion ban caused pregnant woman’s death, lawsuit says
articles.summary: The family of a Texas woman who died from a pregnancy-related complications is suing state Attorney General Ken Paxton and the hospital where she was treated, claiming the state’s ban on most abortions killed her.
articles.body: The family of a Texas woman who died of pregnancy-related complications is suing state officials and the hospital where she was treated, claiming the state’s ban on most abortions killed her. Walker’s family filed a lawsuit in San Antonio on Tuesday, claiming that a doctor repeatedly denied her an abortion despite her having a medical emergency that would have legally permitted terminating the pregnancy. The lawsuit names Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican who is running for election to the U.S. Senate, the Texas Medical Board, which regulates the state’s medical professionals, the University of Texas Health Science ‌Center at ⁠San Antonio and several doctors who treated Walker before she died. “For months, Ms. Walker had been asking for termination of her pregnancy — even though this was a wanted pregnancy — because she did not think she would survive the pregnancy. Tragically, she was right,” the lawsuit states. “An abortion at any point during her pregnancy would have saved her life.” A representative for Paxton did not immediately return NBC News’ request for comment. The Texas Medical Board and the hospital system declined to comment. The hospital where Walker was treated, University Health, said in a statement Thursday that it could not comment on Walker’s case specifically, but that its “priority is to provide medically appropriate and timely care.” “In general, our clinicians make patient care decisions based on each patient’s clinical condition, applicable medical standards and legal requirements,” Elizabeth Allen, a spokesperson for the hospital, said in an email. “We take concerns about patient care seriously and review them through appropriate internal clinical and quality processes.” In September 2024, Walker checked herself into the emergency room at University Health with symptoms of pre-eclampsia, a potentially deadly pregnancy complication, according to the lawsuit. Pre-eclampsia is characterized by high blood pressure and organ failure. It is a leading cause of death among mothers and babies in the United States. The treatment for a severe case of the complication is immediate delivery of the child. However, at 20 weeks pregnant, delivery of Walker’s baby before full term would have been legally considered abortion in Texas. Texas effectively banned all abortions in the state in 2024. Under the law, women can not have an abortion as soon as fetal cardiac activity is detected, which can be as early as five weeks. There are no exceptions for case of rape, incest or fetal anomaly. However, under the law, a physician may perform an abortion when the mother has a life-threatening condition caused by the pregnancy. The lawsuit alleges that when Walker showed those conditions and asked for an abortion, the doctors sent her home. The family is represented by lawyers affiliated with Abortion in America, an advocacy group, and the Marynell Maloney Law Firm. Her family accused doctors of telling Walker “your baby is fine,” and blamed officials for imposing “a merciless blanket prohibition on abortion that intimidates doctors into ​inaction and breeds extreme fear among Texas’ medical establishment.” Walker died in December of that year. She left behind a husband and teenage son. “Tierra, she would have changed the world. And she’s changing it now,” Latanya Walker, one of Tierra Walker’s aunts, said at a press conference Wednesday.
